sentences.text: Plumadraco was a medium-sized enantiornithine bird belonging to the family Bohaiornithidae.
Scientists estimate its body mass fell between 112 and 144 grams.
Fossils show feathers preserved around the wings and tail, including a pair of elongated tail plumes.
The tail featured extremely long feathers roughly twice the body length, ending in distinctive rackets at their tips.
This creature was found in China within the Jiufotang Formation of the Early Cretaceous Aptian age.
Clark and colleagues formally described the species.
The genus contains only one species, P. bankoorum, known from a complete skeleton that preserves soft tissues.
The holotype specimen, the specific example the species is based on, is housed in the Shandong Tianyu Museum of Nature under accession number STM11-4.
Researchers suggest the elongated tail feathers were used primarily for display behavior and courtship rituals.
The authors suggest the holotype specimen belonged to a male based on the likelihood of sexual dimorphism in similar structures.
Plumadraco is classified as a member of Enantiornithes and placed in the family Bohaiornithidae.
Phylogenetic analysis recovered Plumadraco as the sister taxon to an unnamed immature bohaiornithid (CUGB-P1202) within a clade that also includes Sulcavis.
It is difficult to determine the specific selection pressures that shaped ornamental feathers in enantiornithines due to limited soft tissue data.
